page.usage: The chassis: system bar and rail. Also the recessed fill of a payload well inside the pane.

surface.usage: The readout: the pane, and input fields.

map-ground.scope: Scoped exception: the system map pane only. Same value in both themes.

map-core.scope: The orchestrator at the centre of the map. Scoped exception.

map-dormant.scope: An unreachable department and any agent known only from run history. Scoped exception.

map-department.scope: Not a fixed value. One hue per department, evenly spaced from the id-sorted list and rendered oklch(72% 0.16 <hue>). The component passes --hue; the recipe lives in CSS. Scoped exception.

display.purpose: Never standalone. Only the load-bearing figure inside an Answer sentence.

headline.purpose: The pane title, once per pane. Takes the mono family when the title is an account reference.

answer.purpose: The briefing's answer sentences. Regular weight at headline size -- a statement, not a heading.

title.purpose: The wordmark. The only remaining use of this step.

body.purpose: The working size and the document base: rail rows, tables, rationale, form controls.

caption.purpose: Supporting facts, timestamps, rail costs, endpoints, text buttons.

label.purpose: Rail section and block headings and table column headers, in Ash. Also the chip size, un-uppercased.

mono.purpose: Machine values a reader may need to copy exactly: references, endpoints, payloads, raw status codes.

shadows.name: floating-overlay
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system. Chart tooltips. Depth otherwise remains an open decision.

motion.name: slow
motion.purpose: Structural movement: the detail pane sliding over the rail below 900px.

motion.name: breathe
motion.purpose: The live dot while a run is open. Reports that the console is polling.

motion.name: map-travel
motion.value: translate sender -> receiver, linear, infinite; duration = edge length / 240 units per second, clamped 1.2-3.2s
motion.purpose: A dot per handoff edge, running sender to receiver. The one animation in the system that does not report state - a recorded scoped exception. Removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion, since freezing it would leave a permanent speck at each sender.

breakpoints.name: console-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: The only media query. Structural: the rail becomes the whole screen and the pane slides in over it as a detail view.

container.name: system-bar
container.purpose: Fixed chassis, full width, Paper ground.

container.name: rail
container.purpose: Fixed chassis, Paper ground, owns its own scroll.

container.name: pane
container.purpose: The readout. Fluid column on a Card ground, held to a readable measure.

components.name: Rail Row
components.description: One orchestration in the rail. Selection is a background tint plus aria-current -- never a coloured left border.
components.css: .ds-rail { background: var(--page, #f9f9f7); border: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(11,11,11,0.1)); font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; max-width: 340px; } .ds-rail-row { display: block; width: 100%; text-align: left; appearance: none; background: none; border: none; font: inherit; font-size: 13px; color: var(--text-secondary, #52514e); padding: 8px 14px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 140ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0.15,1); } .ds-rail-row:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--text-primary, #0b0b0b) 4%, transparent); } .ds-rail-row[aria-current="true"] { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--series-1, #2470cc) 12%, transparent); color: var(--text-primary, #0b0b0b); } .ds-rail-row:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--series-1, #2470cc); outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-headline { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; justify-content: space-between; } .ds-who { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 12px; color: var(--text-primary, #0b0b0b); } .ds-rail-row[aria-current="true"] .ds-who { font-weight: 600; } .ds-cost { font-size: 12px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--muted, #6e6c66); } .ds-sub { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; margin-top: 3px; font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted, #6e6c66); } .ds-when { margin-left: auto; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; flex: none; } .ds-good { color: var(--good, #0a7c0a); } .ds-attention { color: var(--serious, #b4471a); }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: Five tones. The dot is decoration; the word is the meaning, and the title attribute explains it in a sentence.
components.html: CompletedRunningStopped · repeatingErrorNo verdict
components.css: .ds-chip-row { display: flex; gap: 8px; flex-wrap: wrap; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(11,11,11,0.1)); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-chip::before { content: ''; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; flex: none; } .ds-c-good { color: var(--good, #0a7c0a); } .ds-c-attention { color: var(--serious, #b4471a); } .ds-c-fault { color: var(--critical, #d03b3b); } .ds-c-neutral { color: var(--text-secondary, #52514e); } .ds-c-live { color: var(--series-1, #2470cc); } .ds-c-live::before { animation: ds-breathe 2.4s cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0.15,1) infinite; } @keyframes ds-breathe { 0%,100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.25; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-c-live::before { animation: none; } }

components.name: Block with Answer
components.description: The briefing's unit: a label, a rule, an answer sentence with its figure inline at display size, and a support line.
components.html:
Spend

$0.0656 today, across 3 leads.

$0.0264 per qualified lead, all time$0.0139 per orchestration, all time
components.css: .ds-block { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; padding-top: 22px; border-top: 1px solid var(--grid, #e1e0d9); } .ds-block-label { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: var(--muted, #6e6c66); margin: 0 0 12px; } .ds-answer { font-size: 20px; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.35; letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: var(--text-primary, #0b0b0b); margin: 0; max-width: 46ch; text-wrap: balance; } .ds-fig { font-size: 27px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.02em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-support { margin: 10px 0 0; font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted, #6e6c66); display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 4px 10px; } .ds-sep::before { content: '·'; margin-right: 10px; color: var(--baseline, #c3c2b7); }

components.name: Exception Row
components.description: The attention list. Reference, plain-language explanation, timestamp. Rules between, no box around.
components.css: .ds-exceptions { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-exceptions li + li { border-top: 1px solid var(--grid, #e1e0d9); } .ds-exception { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 12px; width: 100%; text-align: left; appearance: none; background: none; border: none; font: inherit; font-size: 13px; color: inherit; padding: 11px 8px 11px 0; cursor: pointer; transition: background 140ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0.15,1); } .ds-exception:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--series-1, #2470cc) 6%, transparent); } .ds-exception:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--series-1, #2470cc); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 6px; } .ds-exception .ds-who { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 12px; flex: none; } .ds-exception .ds-what { flex: 1; color: var(--text-secondary, #52514e); } .ds-exception .ds-when { font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted, #6e6c66); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; flex: none; }

components.name: Decision Trail
components.description: The signature component. Floating Signal Blue nodes on a rule; three descending registers per step -- decision, reasoning, alternatives.
components.html:
1. 1. Enrichment · marketing
    Lead carries no firmographics; scoring without them produces noise.
    Also considered Scoring, Routing · 31/07/26, 13:55
  2. 2. Stopped here
    Score 5 is far below the disqualify threshold. Terminating without routing.
    Also considered Routing, Outreach draft · 31/07/26, 13:56
components.css: .ds-trail { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-trail li { position: relative; padding: 0 0 20px 26px; border-left: 2px solid var(--grid, #e1e0d9); } .ds-trail li:last-child { border-left-color: transparent; padding-bottom: 0; } .ds-trail li::before { content: ''; position: absolute; left: -6px; top: 4px; width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--series-1, #2470cc); border: 2px solid var(--surface-1, #fcfcfb); } .ds-trail li.ds-terminal::before { background: var(--serious, #b4471a); } .ds-step-agent { font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; color: var(--text-primary, #0b0b0b); } .ds-dept { font-weight: 400; color: var(--muted, #6e6c66); } .ds-step-rationale { color: var(--text-secondary, #52514e); font-size: 13px; margin-top: 2px; max-width: 68ch; } .ds-step-candidates { color: var(--muted, #6e6c66); font-size: 11px; margin-top: 4px; }

components.name: Data Table
components.description: Uppercase Ash headers, hairline dividers, tabular right-aligned figures, one precision per column. No hover -- the rail owns selection.
components.css: .ds-scroll-x { overflow-x: auto; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 13px; color: var(--text-primary, #0b0b0b); } .ds-table th { text-align: left; font-weight: 600; font-size: 11px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: var(--muted, #6e6c66); padding: 8px 14px 8px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(11,11,11,0.1)); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-table td { padding: 10px 14px 10px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--grid, #e1e0d9); vertical-align: top; } .ds-table td:last-child, .ds-table th:last-child { padding-right: 0; } .ds-table .ds-num { text-align: right; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Search Input
components.description: The rail's filter. The placeholder states both behaviours; the label is visually hidden.
components.html: <form class="ds-search" role="search"><label class="ds-vh" for="ds-filter">Filter by account, or press Enter to search every past run</label><input id="ds-filter" class="ds-input" type="search" placeholder="Filter accounts — Enter to search runs" /></form>
components.css: .ds-search { padding: 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(11,11,11,0.1)); background: var(--page, #f9f9f7); display: flex; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-input { font: inherit; font-size: 13px; flex: 1; min-width: 0; padding: 7px 10px; border-radius: 7px; border: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(11,11,11,0.1)); background: var(--surface-1, #fcfcfb); color: var(--text-primary, #0b0b0b); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted, #6e6c66); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--series-1, #2470cc); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-vh { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; clip-path: inset(50%); white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Text Button
components.description: The system's only button form outside the rail. No fill, no border, no radius.
components.css: .ds-linkish { appearance: none; background: none; border: none; padding: 0; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: var(--series-1, #2470cc); cursor: pointer; } .ds-linkish:hover { text-decoration: underline; } .ds-linkish:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--series-1, #2470cc); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 6px; }

components.name: Payload Well
components.description: Recession by inversion: fills with the chassis colour inside the pane, so it reads as cut in rather than raised up.
components.css: .ds-payload { background: var(--page, #f9f9f7); border: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(11,11,11,0.1)); border-radius: 6px; padding: 12px; overflow: auto; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 0; max-height: 340px; color: var(--text-primary, #0b0b0b); }

components.name: System Map
components.description: The scoped dark world. Orchestrator at centre, a hub per department, agents fanned outward. Three tiers of straight edge: trunk, branch, then the handoffs the planner actually made, lightest of all.
components.css: .ds-map { background: radial-gradient(120% 90% at 50% 45%, oklch(19% 0.02 265) 0%, oklch(15% 0.014 265) 55%, oklch(10% 0.012 265) 100%); border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px; } .ds-map-svg { width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; } .ds-map-struct line { stroke: oklch(70% 0.12 var(--h)); } .ds-map-struct line.trunk { stroke-width: 2.5; opacity: 0.55; } .ds-map-struct line.branch { stroke-width: 1.75; opacity: 0.42; } .ds-map-flow path { fill: none; stroke: oklch(78% 0.15 var(--h)); stroke-width: calc(0.75px + var(--w) * 1px); stroke-linecap: round; opacity: calc(0.2 + var(--w) * 0.14); } .ds-map-core { fill: oklch(96% 0.02 250); } .ds-map-hub { fill: oklch(72% 0.16 var(--h)); } .ds-map-node { fill: oklch(74% 0.15 var(--h)); opacity: 0.8; } .ds-map-node.live { fill: oklch(86% 0.15 var(--h)); opacity: 1; animation: ds-map-breathe 2.2s cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0.15,1) infinite; } @keyframes ds-map-breathe { 0%,100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.45; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-map-node.live { animation: none; } }

components.name: Skeleton
components.description: Loading is a shape at the size of the content it replaces, never a spinner in the middle of content.
components.css: .ds-skel-stack { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; } .ds-skeleton { display: inline-block; border-radius: 6px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--grid, #e1e0d9) 0%, color-mix(in srgb, var(--grid, #e1e0d9) 45%, transparent) 50%, var(--grid, #e1e0d9) 100%); background-size: 200% 100%; animation: ds-sweep 1.4s linear infinite; } @keyframes ds-sweep { to { background-position: -200% 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-skeleton { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
This is a calibrated readout, not a dashboard-as-brand-expression. The chassis is a muted warm neutral that asks for nothing; every colored pixel on the screen is a measurement. One accent and four status colors are the entire chromatic budget, and each one means a specific thing. When a surface is grey, it is grey because nothing there needed reporting.

The register is precise, unhurried, understated — confidence through restraint. Type is small and dense but never crowded, figures are tabular so columns of money line up on the decimal, and hierarchy is built almost entirely from weight, case, and colour of text rather than from size jumps.

The second register is calm but alert. The system's job is to leave the reader alone until something needs them: a halted run, an unreachable department, a run that cost more than it should have. Those states get colour that nothing else on the screen is allowed to borrow.

The system is realised as a console: a fixed chassis (system bar and rail) around a single live readout (the pane). There are no tabs and no page navigation. The rail is the bezel and never changes; the pane is what is being measured.
keyCharacteristics: A warm-neutral chassis — off-white with a green-yellow cast, deliberately not blue-grey — with the rail one tonal step recessed from the pane.
One accent (Signal Blue), which marks selection and data and nothing else.
Depth from hairlines and tonal layering; the system is flat with a single overlay shadow.
Text-led hierarchy: uppercase micro-labels, 600/650 weights, tabular figures.
No web fonts, no icon set, no imagery. The system font stack is the whole typographic palette.
Status is always a dot and a word — colour is never the sole carrier of meaning.
Prose carries the answers; the load-bearing figure is set inline at display size.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue is the only non-semantic colour in the interface. It never becomes a large fill, a filled button, a header band, or a brand wash. Its findability is the product — the selected rail row is locatable in peripheral vision precisely because nothing else on the screen is blue. If a new surface wants a second accent, the answer is weight or case, not another hue.

rules.name: The Reserved Signal Rule
rules.body: The four status colours are semantic-only. Nothing decorative may use Clear Green, Hold Amber, Halt Orange, or Fault Red — not a chart series, not a hover state. A reader must be able to assume that orange on this screen means a guardrail fired.

rules.name: The Dark Theme Parity Rule
rules.body: Dark is a peer theme, not a derivative. Every colour token carries both values, and adding one without the other is an incomplete change. Series colours lighten in dark mode; they never darken.

rules.name: The Quiet Heading Rule
rules.body: Headings are smaller and lighter than the content they introduce. An 11px Ash uppercase label sits above a 20px answer sentence. The reader is looking for the answer, not for the word "spend".

rules.name: The Figure-In-Sentence Rule
rules.body: Numbers are not presented as stat tiles. The load-bearing figure is set at display size inside the sentence that explains it, so the number and its meaning are read in one movement and a figure can never appear without its unit of meaning.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that appears in a column is font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums and, in tables, right-aligned. One column uses one precision: costs below a dollar all carry four decimal places, because a column mixing $0.01 and $0.0056 cannot be compared by eye.

rules.name: The Fixed Chassis Rule
rules.body: The bar and the rail never change with selection. Only the pane swaps. A reader who has found a row keeps their place in the list no matter what they open.

rules.name: The Structural Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one media query (900px), and it exists to change structure, not size: below it the rail becomes the whole screen and the pane slides in over it as a detail view with its own back control. Everything else responsive is intrinsic. Reach for intrinsic sizing before adding a second query.

rules.name: The Table Scroll Rule
rules.body: Every table is wrapped in an overflow-x: auto container. A wide table scrolls inside its own block; the page body never scrolls sideways.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Every structural boundary is exactly 1px of alpha-black, never a solid colour and never thicker. The one exception is the decision trail's 2px spine, which is a drawn line rather than a boundary.

rules.name: The No-Container Rule
rules.body: Content is separated by rules and space, not by boxes. Do not reintroduce a card, panel, or tile to group things — a label plus a rule does the same work without adding a border, a radius, a shadow, and an inset to every group on the screen.

rules.name: The Motion-Means-State Rule
rules.body: If an animation is not reporting a state the reader would otherwise have to infer, it does not belong. There are no entrance animations, no scroll choreography, and no page-load sequences — the console loads into a task. Exactly one exception exists, named and scoped under Scoped Exceptions: the map's travelling handoff dots. A second one is not free to appear by pointing at the first.

rules.name: The Scoped Exception Boundary
rules.body: The system map's dark world and generated per-department palette are a recorded exception scoped to .map-stage and nothing else. The four status hues never appear inside it, so the Reserved Signal Rule holds without qualification. A future surface wanting a dark ground or a second accent does not inherit this exception by pointing at it — it argues its own case and gets its own entry, or it uses the system.

dos: Do spend Signal Blue on selection and data only. Its scarcity is the mechanism.
Do give every new colour token both a light and a dark value in the same change, and check it clears 4.5:1 against its own ground in both.
Do render status as a dot and a word, with a plain-language sentence in title.
Do set the load-bearing figure inside the sentence that explains it.
Do use one precision per column — four decimal places below a dollar.
Do separate content with a label and a rule rather than a box.
Do translate halt codes and agent identifiers into outcome language, and keep the raw value reachable in the detail pane's Raw values block.
Do state a below-threshold condition honestly — refuse to draw a chart that would mislead, and say why.
Do keep the chassis fixed when the pane changes.
donts: Don't use Clear Green, Hold Amber, Halt Orange, or Fault Red for anything that isn't status. They are reserved signals.
Don't introduce a second interface accent. If something needs to stand apart, change its weight, case, or size.
Don't reintroduce cards, panels, or tiles. See The No-Container Rule.
Don't add a fourth corner radius. 6 / 7 / 999 covers everything the console has.
Don't mark selection with a coloured left border; use the background tint and aria-current.
Don't thicken the hairline past 1px or make it a solid colour.
Don't add a web font. The native system stack is a deliberate choice.
Don't animate anything that isn't reporting state.
Don't hardcode the three current departments or their agent names. The taxonomy comes from the registry and must absorb a fourth department with no visual change.
Don't read the current flatness as a ban on depth — but if you introduce elevation, introduce a vocabulary, not a one-off shadow.
Don't widen the map's exception past .map-stage.

Don't hardcode a colour, an icon, or a position per department anywhere in the map — hues come from the id-sorted list and positions from the count, which is what lets a new department appear with no frontend edit.

Don't let the map's readout strip size itself from its content. Its height is locked and its rows are clamped precisely because the canvas above it takes the leftover space — a growing strip resizes the constellation on every hover.
Don't treat the map's travelling dots as licence for further decorative motion. They are one named exception to the Motion-Means-State Rule, not a precedent.

Don't rely on prefers-reduced-motion collapsing a duration to disable an animation. An animation whose frozen frame would be wrong — the travelling dots park at the sender — has to be hidden outright.
